propositions: Fault-seeded mutation matrix (seven independent defects: F1–F7) proves the generic reads-under-sync-contention property does not subsume the original regression test; F3 (empty-valid payload) and F6 (incomplete record) are caught only by the original, establishing non-subsumption in one direction.

Reverting the actual slim-fetch-ledge fix (lowering _RECONVERGE_LOCK_TIMEOUT from 15 to 2) leaves both burst tests green; only the deterministic held-lock tests detect the regression, showing the original burst test does not protect against the bug it is named for.

F5 (35s stall) and F7 (empty list surface) are caught only by the generic property, establishing non-subsumption in the reverse direction and confirming both files are complementary oracles rather than duplicates.

Runtime overlap (10.95–22.63s CI variance) is insufficient grounds for consolidation; mutation-score-based criteria (Just et al. FSE 2014) and maintained OSS precedent (Kubernetes, Go, CPython) require proof of behavioral equivalence before deletion is licensed.

Measured wall-clock timings (Ubuntu CI: 12.79–14.93s; macOS local: 8.17–8.76s) confirm the test is expensive but non-eliminable without forfeiting F3/F6 detection; runtime recovery must come from right-sizing the storm (distinct filed ticket) rather than removing the oracle.
